Visit note | 2025-06-25 10:00 AM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Obaidul Mollah, 46, male. Mr. Mollah consults because he noticed swelling of his eyelid along with a painful red lump at the edge of the lid. He is an office cleaner, and he mentions that the problem appeared during a stressful week in Bogura. He has a history of Bronchial asthma but reports no previous eye infections or visual changes. On examination: lump about 5 mm on the left upper eyelid, BP 114/82 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 58 kg. The eye is otherwise quiet with clear cornea and no discharge. Assessment: Hordeolum. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to use a warm compress four times a day, not to squeeze the lump, and to avoid eye makeup. Follow-up in 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 10:30 AM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Mita Ghosh, 55, female. Mrs. Ghosh attends for review regarding her right knee. She reports stiffness in the morning lasting for a few minutes and knee pain when using stairs. She works as a tailor, and her symptoms have become worse since moving to a building with no lift in Narayanganj. She has no significant comorbidity. Interestingly, she describes a sudden locking of the knee with little pain during her daily chores. On examination: BMI 29.6, BP 122/79 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 88 kg. There is mild crepitus and tenderness around the joint line, with stable ligaments. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 10:30 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Rakib Patwary, 45, male. Mr. Patwary attends for review and reports feeling low in energy and experiencing a low mood for over three weeks. He is a ride-share driver, and he explains that his symptoms started after the death of a parent in Cox's Bazar. He has no other medical conditions. The patient denies thoughts of self-harm, and a safety plan with the emergency number 999 was discussed. On examination: PHQ-9 score 12, BP 126/77 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 78 kg. He is cooperative, tearful at times, with congruent affect and intact cognition. Assessment: Depressive episode. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a daily routine, walk outdoors daily, start counselling sessions, and call 999 or come to the clinic at once if thoughts of self-harm appear. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 11:00 AM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Priya Sen, 80, female. Mrs. Sen attends for review and describes passing urine often and losing weight without trying. She works as a shopkeeper, and she notes that her sugar readings rose during a busy season at work in Barishal. She has no known comorbidity and denies any visual disturbances or numbness in her extremities. On examination: fasting glucose 11.7 mmol/L, BP 118/86 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 55 kg. Systemic examination is unremarkable, and peripheral pulses are present. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly 30 minutes five days a week, check fasting sugar twice weekly, and check her feet daily. Follow-up in 3 months with HbA1c.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 11:00 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Marium Begum, 63, female. Mrs. Begum visits because of itchy raised welts that come and go, along with occasional swelling of the lips and symptoms that started after a new food or medicine. She works as a farmer, and she states the trouble started after eating prawns at a restaurant in Shyamoli. She has no chronic illnesses and denies any breathing difficulty. On examination: about 36 welts on the trunk and arms, BP 131/74 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 75 kg. Lungs are clear, and there is no laryngeal edema. Assessment: Acute urticaria. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid the suspected food, keep a symptom diary, and go to hospital at once if the tongue or throat swells. Follow-up in 2 weeks with the symptom diary.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 11:00 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Jamal Bepari, 26, male. Mr. Bepari consults for intermittent swelling of his lips and itchy raised welts that appeared after trying a new food or medicine. He is a tailor, and he notes these symptoms started after eating hilsa at a family dinner in Mohammadpur. He has a history of Bronchial asthma but no prior skin issues. On examination: about 37 welts on the trunk and arms, BP 121/70 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 67 kg. Chest examination reveals mild wheezes consistent with his asthma history, but no respiratory distress. Assessment: Acute urticaria. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid the suspected food, keep a symptom diary, and go to hospital at once if the tongue or throat swells. Follow-up in 2 weeks with the symptom diary.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 11:00 AM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Iffat Mondal, 60, female. Mrs. Mondal returns for review, reporting that she is unable to reach behind her back and suffers from persistent night pain in her shoulder. She is a schoolteacher, and her symptoms began gradually after a long illness in Keraniganj. She has no other chronic medical conditions. On examination: shoulder lifts only to 85 degrees with restricted external rotation, BP 127/85 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 56 kg. Neurological examination of the upper limb is normal. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 11:00 AM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Mahmuda Ahmed, 64, female. Mrs. Ahmed attends for follow-up regarding her itchy eyes and sneezing, which she notes are worse with dust. She is a homemaker, and she explains that her problems flare each spring in Lalbagh. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. On examination: about 10 sneezing fits a day, BP 120/76 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 45 kg. Nasal mucosa appears pale and boggy, and the pharynx is clear. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 11:30 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Jubayer Siddique, 78, male. Mr. Siddique presents with complaints of getting tired easily and experiencing dizzy spells. He works as a tailor, and he mentions that his symptoms started after a sleepless night travelling to Tejgaon. He has no other major health problems. On examination: pulse 134 bpm and irregular, BP 134/80 mmHg, weight 83 kg. Heart sounds are irregularly irregular with no added murmurs, and lung fields are clear. Assessment: Atrial fibrillation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to limit tea and coffee, avoid alcohol, and report any fainting at once. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and kidney function tests.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 11:30 AM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Jewel Mollah, 63, male. Mr. Mollah returns for follow-up because his breathlessness has been worse for several days, accompanied by wheezing on walking and more sputum than usual. He is a homemaker, and his condition worsened during the dusty dry season in Gulshan. He has a known history of Bronchial asthma. Notably, he exhibits mild confusion and sleepiness with only mild breathlessness during the consultation. On examination: SpO2 87%, BP 130/85 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 47 kg. Chest auscultation reveals diffuse expiratory wheezes and reduced air entry. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 12:00 PM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Habib Kabir, 63, male. Mr. Kabir visits for the first time complaining of dizzy spells and an irregular fast heartbeat. On examination: pulse 142 bpm and irregular, BP 131/86 mmHg, weight 50 kg. Auscultation confirms an irregularly irregular rhythm, and his chest has scattered wheezes from his asthma. Assessment: Atrial fibrillation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to limit tea and coffee, avoid alcohol, and report any fainting at once. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and kidney function tests.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 12:30 PM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Chandana Paul, 51, female. On examination: about 10 headache days a month, BP 113/70 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, weight 94 kg. Neurological examination is normal with no focal deficits. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up in 3 months with the headache diary.

Visit note | 2025-06-25 03:30 PM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Gautam Chakraborty, 31, male. Visit note | 2025-06-25 04:00 PM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Mahmuda Bhuiyan, 26, female. Ms. Bhuiyan consults because her stools switch between loose and hard, accompanied by cramping belly pain that is worse with stress. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-06-26 02:00 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Saad Shikder, 23, male. Visit note | 2025-06-26 02:30 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Mala Saha, 20, female. Visit note | 2025-06-26 03:00 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Karim Kabir, 38, male. Mr. Kabir attends for follow-up reporting severe scratching at night and skin symptoms that are worse in winter. On examination: affected area about 10 cm across, BP 112/73 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 85 kg. Skin lesions show dry, erythematous plaques in the flexural creases with mild excoriations. Visit note | 2025-06-26 03:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Puja Paul, 61, female. Mrs. Paul consults for back pain, noting stiffness when bending and discomfort that eases with rest. She works as a hotel receptionist, and her symptoms started after carrying a gas cylinder up the stairs in Dhanmondi. She has Essential hypertension. On examination: pain score 5/10, BP 141/91 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 71 kg. There is localized muscle spasm and tenderness in the lumbar spine with preserved range of motion. Assessment: Lumbar muscle strain. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to stay gently active, use a warm compress, and lift with the knees bent. Follow-up in 2 weeks if the pain continues.

Visit note | 2025-06-26 03:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Habiba Awal, 62, female. Mrs. Awal presents with worry about her sleep, waking up tired, and trouble falling asleep most nights. Visit note | 2025-06-26 03:30 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Mehedi Shikder, 52, male. Mr. Shikder visits for a first evaluation, reporting no specific symptoms but noting a family history where his father had a heart attack at 55, along with high cholesterol found on a routine test. Visit note | 2025-06-26 03:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Bilkis Majumder, 48, female. On examination: reduced sensation at 5 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 118/84 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, weight 78 kg. Ankle reflexes are diminished bilaterally. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Visit note | 2025-06-26 03:30 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Parvin Alam, 26, female. Visit note | 2025-06-26 04:30 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Emon Ahmed, 25, male. Mr. Ahmed presents with fever and painful swallowing. Visit note | 2025-06-26 04:30 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Sohel Dewan, 26, male. Mr. Dewan attends for review reporting gritty burning eyes and long hours of screen time.
